title: Same Score, 3x The Bill
caption:
Your agent harness doesn't decide whether it works. It decides what you pay.

Five models, three harnesses, SWE-bench Verified. Claude Code and mini-SWE-agent — heaviest and lightest — land within five points. Swapping harness flips 13% of tasks; rerunning the same one, changing nothing, flips 13% too. Cost per task: up to 3x apart.

I switched harnesses twice this year chasing pass rates. Turns out I was shopping for a bill, not a score.

Which harness are you on?

slides.headline:
Same Score,
3x The Bill
slides.sub: Five models through three agent harnesses on SWE-bench Verified. Pass rates land within five points of each other. Cost per task runs up to 3x apart. Shandong University preprint, 7 October 2026.

slides.title: Heaviest Ties Lightest
slides.sub: On 447 SWE-bench Verified tasks, Claude Code — the heaviest harness tested — lands within five points of mini-SWE-agent, the lightest.

slides.headline: 13% Either Way
slides.sub: On a 45-task hard subset with five models, swapping the harness flips 13% of tasks. Rerunning the same harness, changing nothing, flips 13% too. And the tasks a harness wins in one run are not the ones it wins in the next.

slides.headline:
The Preamble
Is The Bill
slides.sub: The 3x gap is set at the first call. Every harness resends its system prompt and tool schemas with each step, multiplied by the number of steps. Per-step growth and tool output differ far less.

slides.title: What This Doesn’t Say
items: SWE-bench Verified only. Nothing here about your repo.
One harness does lose: OpenCode trails by up to 9 points.
On one model, half that gap is runs cut short by its output cap.
447 tasks resolve 5 points — coarser than many claimed gains.
A preprint posted 7 October 2026. Not peer reviewed.
